title: Sausage Rolls
subtitle: British flaky puff pastry sausage rolls
excerpt: The definitive British sausage roll: herbed pork sausagemeat wrapped in all-butter puff pastry, glazed with egg wash, and baked until the pastry is deeply golden and flaky. Essential at any gathering.

recipe.sourceNotes: Sausage rolls are one of the most beloved British baked goods, found in every bakery, supermarket, and party buffet. They consist of seasoned pork sausagemeat wrapped in puff pastry and baked until golden. The sausagemeat filling is typically seasoned more aggressively than a regular sausage: more herbs, pepper, and aromatics, since the pastry needs flavour to come through. The best sausage rolls use proper all-butter puff pastry, not the cheaper margarine-based varieties; the difference in flavour and texture is substantial. Adding a small amount of finely diced shallot and English mustard to the filling produces the best result. Sausage rolls freeze very well before baking; bake from frozen, adding 5 minutes to the cooking time.

content.text: Keep the pastry cold until the moment it goes in the oven; warm pastry does not rise as well and the butter leaks out. Season the filling aggressively; wrapped in pastry, it needs more salt and pepper than you think. Chill the assembled rolls for 30 minutes before baking for the best rise.

content.text: Mix the pork mince with the shallots, mustard, thyme, sage, salt, and pepper until well combined. Fry a small piece in a pan to taste the seasoning; adjust if needed.

Roll the pastry into a large rectangle about 3 mm thick. Cut into two long strips. Place a log of filling (about 5 cm diameter) along one long edge of each strip. Roll the pastry over the filling and seal the edge with egg wash, pressing to secure. Seam-side down. Brush the tops with egg wash. Cut into 8 to 10 cm lengths. Score the tops with a knife.
Chill for 30 minutes. Preheat the oven to 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6. Bake for 25 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the filling is cooked through.
